subject: Payment terms & rate card request for Hosted API
messages:
From: J. Patel <j.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2025-04-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Rate card + billing cadence question

Hi Rishi,

We're evaluating Redwood's Hosted API for a new internal search augmentation project and would like to understand two things before we move to procurement: 1) your current public rate card / baseline pricing for hosted API (token pricing, embeddings, any seat or QPS packaging), and 2) billing cadence — do you support monthly invoicing on net terms (Net 30) or is payment by corporate card required?

Other context: we expect roughly $20k-40k of monthly usage initially and are open to a 12-month committed arrangement if there are committed-volume discounts. Procurement wants to know whether discounts can be applied up front and whether they'd be retroactive to the start of the paid term. Our timeline is tight — we want a PO in-hand within two weeks if possible.

Can you share a quick rate card and outline the process for setting up monthly invoicing and net terms? Also note any documentation procurement will need (W-9, contract, credit form, etc.).

Thanks,
J. (Jay) Patel
Head of Procurement
Acme Corp
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: J. Patel <j.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-09T12:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + billing cadence question

Hi Jay — thanks for the note and the context. Quick answers up front, and then a suggested next step:

1) Rate card: attaching a concise rate sheet (Redwood_rate_card_v2.xlsx) that shows hosted API baseline list prices for generation and embeddings plus our standard volume tiers. Baseline examples: 0.6¢/1k tokens for gpt-style small models, 2.4¢/1k tokens for high-capacity variants; embeddings at $0.0015/unit — see attachment for full table.

2) Billing cadence and net terms: default is card on file for self-serve accounts. For enterprise customers we offer monthly invoicing on Net 30 or Net 45 after a credit check and an executed commercial agreement (MSA + ordering document or SOW). Setup items typically required by Finance: W-9 (US), signed MSA, PO referencing the Redwood deal id, and a simple credit application if net terms are requested.

Discounts: we do provide committed-volume discounts for 12-month terms. Typical range is 10–20% depending on committed ARR and cadence. For your volume band (est. $20k–40k/mo) I can propose a 15% committed discount pending final volumes and legal/finance signoff. Discounts are applied to the billed usage starting from the effective date in the SOW — we can make them retroactive to the paid start date on request, but need that in the ordering docs.

Next step: I will loop in our finance lead (Marissa) to handle invoicing setup and a short checklist for procurement. If you can share the PO template and expected start date we can draft an ordering document and quote.

Attaching: Redwood_rate_card_v2.xlsx (summary table).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Rate card + billing cadence question — please advise on Net 30 for Acme

Marissa — forwarding Acme's ask. TL;DR: expected start ASAP, estimated $20–40k/mo, requesting monthly invoicing on Net 30 and 15% committed discount for 12 months. Procurement wants PO within two weeks. Can you confirm what we need from them and whether we can offer Net 30 prior to a credit application?

Specifics I need from Finance:
- Approvals required for Net 30 for a first-time customer at ~$300k ARR run rate
- Any limits on invoice aging before requiring a card on file
- Whether discounts can be applied retroactively to the paid start date or must start at invoice issuance
- Draft invoice cadence (day invoices generated, due date, remittance instructions) and whether ACH/wire preferred

If easier, happy to set up a 15-minute call with Jay + procurement.

Thanks,
Rishi
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, J. Patel <j.patel@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2025-04-10T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rate card + billing cadence question — please advise on Net 30 for Acme

Hi team — copying finance details below so procurement has what they need. Short answer: yes, we can do monthly invoicing on Net 30 for Acme pending standard onboarding checks.

Checklist / required items from Acme for Net 30 setup:
- Signed MSA (or fully signed SOW referencing MSA)
- PO that references our deal id (RWI-2024-ACM-17)
- Completed credit application (one-pager)
- W-9 (if US entity) or equivalent tax form

Invoicing cadence and mechanics:
- Invoices generated on the 1st of the month for the prior month's usage (usage 2025-05-01 invoice covers Apr usage).
- Standard terms: Net 30 from invoice date.
- Preferred payment methods: ACH/wire. We accept credit card for the first 1–2 months while Net 30 is being enabled, but we prefer ACH for recurring invoices to avoid processing fees.
- Late payment: interest at 1.5%/month after 30 days; we escalate to account hold after 60 days past due.

Discounts and retroactivity:
- Committed discounts can be applied as of the SOW effective date. If Acme wants the discount retroactive to an earlier paid trial period, we can include retroactivity in the SOW but need explicit language and finance approval.

Attachments: proposed_net30_invoice.pdf (example invoice and billing setup checklist).

Operational notes for Rishi: for a new Net 30 setup at ~$20–40k/mo we will: run the credit app (2–3 business days), validate W-9, get signed MSA/SOW, then enable Net 30 in billing system. If procurement needs the PO sooner, we can provision with card for first invoice and switch to invoice billing once onboarding is complete.

Let me know if you'd like me to prepare the formal quote (with the 15% commit discount outlined) and the SOW template.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance, Redwood Inference
